This lesson has no matching ART.scene (the kit keeps no top-level 'machines/robots/factory' drawing), so every picture here is drawn in the engine's own idiom, the way tools/lib/film-scenes/computing-g3/networks-around-us.js draws its hardware: nothing is borrowed from the kit except the word-for-word wording of its explanations. title: Machines, Things and Robots
subtitle: Grade 3 Computing
objectives: Know that computers can be programmed to control machines and other physical objects.
Identify common 'Internet of Things' devices in a familiar environment.
Explain the role of robots in manufacturing.

beats.say: Some machines have a program deciding what they do.

at.program: a program deciding what they do

beats.say: Some things talk to the internet, and robots build cars in factories.
A program controls a machine when a small computer inside decides what it does: it is computer-controlled.
A washing machine runs a program: it decides when to turn, heat and stop.

at.washing1: A washing machine runs a program

beats.say: Traffic lights and a lift have programs too. An automatic door opens for a sensor.
A bicycle, a whisk and a broom have no program. You do all the work.

at.bicyclewhiskbroom: A bicycle, a whisk and a broom

beats.say: So ask: is a computer deciding, or are you?
A bulb, a doorbell, a thermostat, a plug.
Add a small computer inside, connected to the internet.
That is an Internet of Things device: a smart device.
Smart does not mean clever. It means connected.
A smart watch counts your steps and sends them to your phone.
A smart bulb switches on from your phone, even from another town.
The lamp beside it, with a switch, is not smart.
Robots weld the car's metal body, then paint it.
A robot lifts the engine in, then fits the doors and the wheels.
People test the finished car.
Six steps, most of them done by a robot.
Exact. A robot welds in the same place, to the millimetre, every time.
Heavy. An engine is too heavy to lift. A robot arm lifts it in.
Dangerous. Paint fumes and hot metal are safer for a robot.
Repeated: the same repetitive step, ten thousand times a day, and it never gets tired.
And the people: they program each robot, check every car, and fix what breaks.
Robots did not take all the jobs. They do the steps; people run the factory.

at.nottakejobs1: did not take all the jobs

beats.say: The program decides: move here, weld, move back.
The motors are outputs. They move the arm where the program says.
The sensors are inputs. They tell the program where the arm is.

at.tellwhere1: tell the program where the arm is

beats.say: The stop button is an input too. Press it, and every motor stops.
A factory robot is a computer controlling a machine, just like the automatic door.
A program can control a machine, deciding what it does.

at.control4: A program can control a machine

beats.say: Everyday things that connect to the internet are the Internet of Things.
Robots do the exact, heavy, dangerous and repeated jobs in a factory.
And a robot is a computer controlling a machine: sensors in, motors out.
